title: Monotonicity of the postcondition
statement: Let $L$ be resource limits, $s$ a statement, $\sigma$ a state, and $R,R'$ predicates on states. If $s$ is block-safe from $\sigma$ and its resulting state satisfies $R$, and every state satisfying $R$ also satisfies $R'$, then $s$ is block-safe from $\sigma$ and its resulting state satisfies $R'$.
replaced:
Let $\mathrm{lim}$ be a set of word, space, and depth bounds, let $s$ be a statement,
and let $\sigma$ be a program state. If $s$ runs safely from $\sigma$ to a postcondition
$R$, and every state satisfying $R$ also satisfies a postcondition $R'$, then $s$ runs
safely from $\sigma$ to $R'$.
